name: Sonoff ZBMINI-L2 (EU)

radios.note: Zigbee 3.0 end device; it does not relay Zigbee traffic for other devices.

matter.note: No Matter claim found on Sonoff's pages and no CSA Matter listing found. Not treated as 'no'.

apple_home.note: Sonoff's help centre does not list Apple Home.

google_home.via: SONOFF Zigbee gateway (e.g. ZBBridge-P, NSPanel Pro, iHost)
google_home.note: Sonoff says voice control works with Google Assistant once the switch is on a Zigbee gateway in eWeLink; the gateway-to-Google path is not spelled out per gateway.

alexa.note: Sonoff's list names Echo Plus 2nd gen, Echo 4th gen and Echo Show 2nd gen as supported Zigbee gateways.

smartthings.via: SmartThings Hub V3 / Aeotec Hub V3
smartthings.note: Listed by Sonoff as a supported gateway.

home_assistant.note: Sonoff lists ZBDongle-P and ZBDongle-E with ZHA or Zigbee2MQTT. Needs a coordinator; Philips, IKEA and Fritzbox gateways are not supported.

hubRequired.note: Needs a Zigbee 3.0 gateway such as the SONOFF ZBBridge, NSPanel Pro, iHost or a supported Echo or SmartThings hub.

localControl.note: Sonoff's pages say it works with local-capable gateways, but no page states local control explicitly.

switchForm.note: 39.5 x 32 x 18.4 mm relay for the back box of an existing switch, with S1/S2 inputs for the wall switch.

neutralRequired.note: Sold as no-neutral; the lamp's own neutral is used. Minimum load is about 3 W and flash suppression modules are not supported.

gangs.note: Sonoff's pages describe one relay output with S1/S2 switch inputs but don't state a channel or gang count; only retailers say single-channel.

summary: The Sonoff ZBMINI-L2, also sold as ZBMINI Extreme, is a small Zigbee relay for a switch box with no neutral wire. It switches up to 6 A at 100-240 V and supports two-way switching from an external wall switch. It needs a Zigbee gateway, and Sonoff lists compatible ones for eWeLink, Alexa, SmartThings and Home Assistant.
caveats: Needs a Zigbee 3.0 gateway; Philips Hue, IKEA and Fritzbox gateways are not supported.
It is an end device and does not extend your Zigbee mesh.
No-neutral operation needs a minimum load of about 3 W and does not support flash suppression modules.
The ZBMINIL2-E in Sonoff's docs is a different, larger model.
